lines.text: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are going on a big trip!
Every animal has a home. Some homes are hot. Some homes are cold.
Three animal friends are coming with us. One, two, three!
Let's find out where they live. Are you ready? Let's go!
Where does the arctic fox live?
Does the arctic fox live here, in the hot, sandy desert?
No! Too hot for a fluffy fox. Let's try again.
The arctic fox lives in the snowy Arctic! Brrr!
Here is the fun fact. In winter, the arctic fox is white, like the snow.
But in summer, when the snow melts, its fur turns brown!
White in winter, to hide in the snow. Brown in summer, to hide in the rocks.
But how does a little fox stay warm in all that snow?
At bedtime, it wraps its fluffy tail around itself, like a blanket!
And it has thick fur under its paws, like snow boots!
The arctic fox lives at the very top of the world, where it is cold almost all year.
When a snowstorm comes, the fox digs a den in the snow, and stays cozy inside.
Say it with me. White in winter, brown in summer!
Can you curl up like a fox in the snow? Curl, curl, curl!
Quick check! What color is the arctic fox in winter? White? Or brown?
White! White like the snow.
Wave bye-bye to the fluffy fox. Bye-bye, fox!
Where does the monkey live?
Does the monkey live here, in the warm, rainy jungle?
Yes! The monkey lives in the jungle!
Here is the fun fact. Many monkeys live high up in the jungle trees.
They eat in the trees, play in the trees, and sleep in the trees!
Why do monkeys like the trees so much?
Up in the trees there are sweet fruits, crunchy leaves, nuts, and seeds. Yum!
Some monkeys can even hold on to a branch with their tail, like an extra hand!
Monkeys live together in a big group. A group of monkeys is called a troop.
Can you say troop?
They travel together all day, looking for food.
A troop can be small, with just a few monkeys. Or very, very big!
Trees are a monkey's kitchen, playground, and bedroom!
Say it with me. Monkeys live in the trees!
Can you swing your arms like a monkey? Swing, swing, swing!
Quick check! Where do many monkeys live? Up in the trees? Or under the sea?
Up in the trees! Super!
Wave bye-bye to the monkey. Bye-bye, monkey!
Where does the brown bear live?
Does the bear live here, in the hot, sandy desert?
No! Too hot for a furry bear. Let's try again.
The brown bear lives in the mountain forest!
How does a bear get ready for the cold winter?
Before winter comes, the bear eats, and eats, and eats! It gets nice and round.
Here is the fun fact. In winter, many bears sleep in a cozy den.
They snooze through the cold, snowy days, until spring comes back.
And here is a surprise. Baby bears are born in the den, in the middle of winter!
Baby bears are called cubs.
The tiny cubs snuggle close to their mama until spring.
The den keeps the bear family warm in the snow.
Can you say den?
In spring, the bear family comes out of the den. Time to find some food!
Say it with me. Bears sleep in a den in winter!
Can you yawn and stretch like a sleepy bear? Yawn. Stretch!
Quick check! Where do many bears sleep in winter? In a den? Or in a tree?
In a den! Cozy and warm.
Sleep well, sleepy bear!
Wow! We visited three animal homes. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
Who lives in the snowy Arctic, and turns brown in summer?
The arctic fox! Yes!
Who lives high in the jungle trees?
The monkey! Good job!
And who sleeps in a den in winter?
The bear! You remembered!
You learned so many new things today.
Curl up like a fox. Swing like a monkey. And stretch like a bear!
Where is your home? Is it hot or cold today?
Thank you for traveling with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
